title: A member is never told about the snapshots it was given
foundBy: user report (host), relaying a reviewing agent: the orientation names a member's repositories but not its snapshots
details:
A member is told about its repositories and never about its snapshots, though both are directories placed in its home.

`--repo` and `--snapshot` are siblings in cs-sandbox. Each shares a directory into the guest at `~/<name>`, and cs-campaign derives that name the same way for both. A repository arrives as a writable clone on the member's own branch. A snapshot arrives as a frozen read-only copy.

The orientation lists the repositories under "What you have" and stops. `member.json` carries the repositories with their base commits, and carries no snapshots at all. A member holding a reference tree therefore has no way to learn that it exists, short of listing its home directory.

The orchestrator is told. Its `manifest.json` gives every agent's roster row that agent's snapshots. The product treats a snapshot as worth knowing for the seat that allocates work, and not for the seat that holds it.

R13 names frozen snapshots among what each member can see. R31 says a member's knowledge must be exactly its trees, its seeded input and its dispatches, and that the enumeration is what makes the question answerable. A snapshot is a tree the member was given, and nothing enumerates it to the member.

The cost is quiet. An operator who shares a reference tree and expects it to be read must name it in the brief. Naming a path the product could have stated is the guesswork SAC-006 removed everywhere else.
